label: Cover
caption: Lion’s mane, turmeric, and ginkgo: three extraordinary organisms, three very different paths through scientific research.
alt: Lion’s mane mushrooms beside glowing orange turmeric rhizomes and golden ginkgo leaves against a deep-green science-inspired background, with Mindful Diabetes Inc. branding.

label: Figure 1
caption: Brain insulin signaling, glucose use, and vascular or inflammatory influences are related but different biological processes. This is a conceptual illustration, not a diagnostic algorithm.
alt: Mindful Diabetes science diagram with separate panels explaining insulin signaling in the brain, glucose utilization, and vascular or immune influences.

label: Figure 2
caption: Cardiometabolic risk, Alzheimer-associated pathology, and cognitive symptoms overlap in some people but are not interchangeable. Diabetes does not inevitably cause Alzheimer pathology.
alt: Three-part Mindful Diabetes schematic distinguishing metabolic and vascular risk factors, Alzheimer-associated pathological changes, and cognitive outcomes or dementia syndromes.

label: Figure 3
caption: The visible fruiting body and threadlike mycelium are different fungal structures. Study preparations can vary in their chemical composition; a common ingredient name does not identify a standardized exposure.
alt: Side-by-side illustration of white lion’s mane fruiting bodies and a labeled branching mycelium network, with notes on compound families studied in each.

label: Figure 4
caption: Lion’s mane compounds are studied for possible roles in neurotrophic signaling. These proposed pathways do not establish a neurological benefit in people; an acute 18-person 2025 study found no significant overall cognitive benefit.
alt: Mindful Diabetes lion’s mane diagram depicting hericenones, erinacines, exploratory neurotrophic pathways, and an 18-person human trial summary.

label: Figure 5
caption: Species identification, material used, extraction, formulation, and quality evaluation all matter. Products carrying the same common name may not be chemically or clinically equivalent.
alt: Five-step infographic showing how organism identification, chosen biological material, extraction, formulation, and quality checks affect a supplement product.

label: Figure 6
caption: Curcumin’s journey through digestion, absorption, metabolism, and circulation helps explain why activity in a cell dish does not predict clinical benefit or safety.
alt: A turmeric pharmacokinetics diagram showing ingestion, intestinal absorption, liver metabolism, circulation, and possible tissue exposure.

label: Figure 7
caption: Published GEM trial estimates: all-cause dementia hazard ratio 1.12 (95% CI 0.94–1.33) and Alzheimer dementia 1.16 (95% CI 0.97–1.39). Neither outcome showed statistically established prevention benefit.
alt: Forest plot of the Ginkgo Evaluation of Memory randomized trial; both confidence intervals include the null hazard ratio of one.

label: Figure 8
caption: Natural-product inspiration and clinically approved medicines are different stages of discovery: the chemical history of metformin includes goat’s rue, while the synthetic GLP-1 medicine exenatide grew from Gila monster peptide research.
alt: Two illustrated medicinal chemistry stories linking Galega officinalis to metformin history and the Gila monster peptide exendin-4 to synthetic exenatide.

label: Figure 9
caption: A memory task, a test of executive function, a self-reported symptom, and a clinical diagnosis answer different research questions. Improvement on a test is not the same as preventing dementia.
alt: Four comparison cards depicting memory tasks, executive function, self-reported experiences, and clinically important cognitive outcomes.

label: Figure 10
caption: From cellular studies to controlled human trials, each research design answers a different question. Strong claims need evidence suited to the claim and the population.
alt: Scientific evidence map separating laboratory experiments, animal models, small human studies, and larger controlled clinical trials.

label: Figure 11
caption: Bioactive does not necessarily mean safe. Limited long-term data for lion’s mane, turmeric-associated liver injury reports, and ginkgo–medication interactions deserve attention.
alt: Three-column Mindful Diabetes safety infographic comparing uncertainties for lion’s mane, concentrated turmeric extracts, and ginkgo leaf extracts.

label: Figure 12
caption: Evidence-informed brain-health priorities include movement, cardiovascular care, individualized diabetes management, not smoking, hearing care, and social connection. No checklist guarantees prevention.
alt: Six illustrated cards showing activity, blood-pressure management, diabetes care, smoking avoidance, hearing care, and social connection.
